header: Date: 2027-09-09 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Jordan Meyer (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE); Marta Delgado (LatchPoint CTO), Samir Patel (DevOps), Lena Cho (ML Engineer), Tom Brooks (Product)
summary: Implementation kickoff checkpoint focused on readiness for a 3-week pilot. Main topics: VPC and network connectivity, staging vs prod rollout plan, benchmark scope (latency/cost targets), data retention and compliance handoff. Agreed next steps for docs, sample traffic, and benchmark scheduling.
topics: Staging API key handoff and SSO
transcript: [00:00] Jordan Meyer: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we wanted to run a short activation pulse and make sure we're aligned for the pilot
[00:12] Marta Delgado: thanks jordan, we have about 45 minutes, want to focus on network/setup and then bench plan
[00:20] Priya Shah: perfect, i'll share the runbook in chat after the call — it covers staging keys, roles, and the typical sequence we follow

[00:30] Samir Patel: quick context — we're running EKS in us-west-2, all outbound egress through our NAT gateways, and we have strict egress for compliance, so VPC peering or PrivateLink is preferable
[00:45] Ethan Wu: got it, we can support PrivateLink and VPC peering. for the pilot do you want hosted with private networking or dedicated capacity?
[00:55] Lena Cho: from model ops side we want deterministic latency, at least 95th percentile under 250ms for short chat flows. cost is a concern but SLA first for the pilot
[01:10] Tom Brooks: product wants canary routing to a small subset of users first, so we'll need separate staging and prod routes
[01:25] Jordan Meyer: recommended path — start hosted with VPC-only routing to isolate traffic, then evaluate Dedicated if throughput or latency variance shows up in bench results
[01:40] Marta Delgado: curious about KV cache and prefix caching — are those preserved across routing variants? we've got some long context workloads

[01:50] Ethan Wu: good question — prefix and KV cache behavior is runtime-specific; we can configure session affinity on the Redwood side for the pilot so cache hits are stable. we'll include that in the benchmark plan
[02:05] Priya Shah: i'm writing notes; i'll add cache strategy to the runbook for the pilot. also i'll include contact points and escalation SOP
[02:20] Samir Patel: regarding security — we need details for KMS integration and also for audit logs. our security team will request a SOC2 artifact pack
[02:35] Jordan Meyer: we'll send the SOC2 summary and a secure artifact bundle. Priya, can you own the compliance packet handoff?
[02:42] Priya Shah: yes, i'll assemble and share with Marta's security contact. need the contact email after the call
[03:00] Marta Delgado: i'll DM you our security lead — note we also need data retention options (30/90/365 days) and the ability to purge on request
[03:12] Ethan Wu: Redwood supports configurable retention windows and a purge API. we'll document retention configs and demo the purge on the pilot staging environment
[03:30] Tom Brooks: timeline check — we want the pilot to start in two weeks and run for three weeks. is that feasible?
[03:38] Jordan Meyer: yes, that's reasonable. two-week ramp to get staging and keys, then 3-week pilot. benchmarks should be scheduled during week 1 of pilot
[03:50] Lena Cho: for benchmarks we'll provide two prompt sets: conversational short-turns and multi-turn long context. also we'll send expected QPS/peak windows
[04:05] Samir Patel: our nightly batch runs spike some traffic, peak qps is around 120 during batch — but it's bursty. we'd like autoscaling to handle those bursts without cold starts
[04:20] Ethan Wu: will note burst profile. Redwood's autoscaler and warm pool can be tuned; for pilot we'll set up a small warm pool and measure cold-start penalties in the bench
[04:35] Jordan Meyer: on pricing — i'll send the pilot pricing worksheet, but for the pilot we'll provide a cost estimate and credits depending on scope
[04:45] Marta Delgado: appreciated — procurement will want a line-item for a reserved eval if we consider Dedicated later
[04:55] Tom Brooks: about SSO, we use Okta. need SAML config and a service account in staging to validate role-based access
[05:05] Priya Shah: we support Okta SAML; please share the IdP metadata URL and the groups you want mapped, i'll coordinate with our identity team
[05:20] Samir Patel: note that our infra folks need an IP allowlist for the staging peering; do you have a list of egress addresses?

[05:30] Ethan Wu: for PrivateLink we'll provide the endpoint configuration; for VPC peering we can provide the CIDR ranges. we'll avoid publishing wide egress lists until we finalize the connection method
[05:45] Lena Cho: small question on model versions — can we pin a model revision and rollback automatically if quality regressions occur?
[05:55] Jordan Meyer: yes, rollouts are configurable — canary + auto rollback on quality/regression signals. we can instrument eval hooks into your prompt sets to trigger a rollback
[06:10] Marta Delgado: good — we need about 2 rollback playbooks: one for perf regressions and one for hallucination/quality
[06:25] Priya Shah: i'll add rollback playbooks to the runbook and include sample alerts and thresholds
[06:40] Tom Brooks: for operations, who owns runbook execution during pilot? internal LatchPoint or Redwood on-call?
[06:50] Jordan Meyer: typical model is shared ops — Redwood handles platform-level incidents, LatchPoint handles product-level changes. we'll list operation handoffs explicitly in runbook
[07:05] Samir Patel: also want a health-check dashboard and a daily digest for the pilot, token-level cost and latency breakdowns
[07:15] Ethan Wu: Redwood Console can provide per-route dashboards and a daily report. i'll prepare a demo snapshot for your team in staging
[07:30] Marta Delgado: can we see an example of the daily digest? that helps us anticipate cost spikes
[07:38] Priya Shah: i'll attach a sample digest to the runbook package. it's fairly lightweight and configurable
[07:50] Jordan Meyer: let's confirm benchmark metrics: p50/p95 latency, median token cost, throughput, cache hit rate, and cold-start frequency. anything else?
[08:05] Lena Cho: add output quality metrics (BLEU-ish or custom eval on our prompt sets) and hallucination rate thresholds
[08:18] Tom Brooks: and a small user-level error budget tied to rollout — e.g., if error rate > X revert canary
[08:28] Jordan Meyer: noted. we'll include thresholds and alerting rules in the bench plan
[08:40] Marta Delgado: legal note — we need a redaction policy for PII that flows to Redwood logs. do you support configurable scrubbing?
[08:52] Ethan Wu: yes, we support pre-ingest scrubbing hooks and token-level redaction. we'll show recommended patterns in the runbook
[09:05] Samir Patel: for production rollout, if we need Dedicated, what's the procurement lead time?
[09:13] Jordan Meyer: dedicated pool provisioning typical lead is 4-6 weeks after contract; pilot helps validate whether Dedicated is needed
[09:25] Marta Delgado: okay that matches our calendar. final Q: who is the day-to-day POC?
[09:32] Priya Shah: i'm the CSM lead and primary onboarding POC; Jordan AE will own commercial/contract items; Ethan will own benchmarks/SE work
[09:42] Tom Brooks: perfect, Priya — i'll copy you on the security contact email after the call
[09:50] Jordan Meyer: recap: Priya sends runbook & SOC2 pack, Ethan drafts bench plan, Samir shares traffic histograms and Okta metadata, Marta confirms security lead. agreed dates in next steps
[10:08] Marta Delgado: yes agreed. thanks everyone — excited to get this moving
[10:15] Jordan Meyer: thanks team, we'll follow up with links and schedule the benchmark session. end call
[10:18] (meeting ends)
